items.q: A factory has capacity of 180 units a day and capacity utilisation of 80%. It has 16 employees, each paid £60 a day. The selling price is £15 per unit and all output is sold. Calculate employee costs as a percentage of turnover.
items.why: Output = 80% × 180 = 144 units a day. Turnover = 144 × £15 = £2,160 a day. Employee costs = 16 × £60 = £960 a day. £960 ÷ £2,160 × 100 = 44.4%. Using full capacity (£2,700) gives 35.6%, which is wrong.
items.label: Paper 1 November 2020 Q17

items.q: Revenue £150k, Cost of sales £80k, Expenses £50k. Gross profit = ?
items.why: Gross profit = Revenue - Cost of Sales = 150 - 80 = £70,000. Same rule every time: Gross profit = Revenue - Cost of Sales only.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Use the break-even chart. What is the break-even output?
items.why: Break-even is where the total revenue and total costs lines cross, at 500 units. You can check: fixed costs £2,500 ÷ contribution per unit of £5 = 500 units.

items.q: A business has inventory of £130,000, total current assets of £380,000 and current liabilities of £520,000. What is its current ratio?
items.why: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = £380,000 ÷ £520,000 = 0.73:1. Inventory is already part of current assets, so it is not taken off.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has a 40% share of a market. The market grows by 10% and the business's sales stay the same. What is its new market share?
items.why: Take the market as 100 before the change. The business sells 40. The market becomes 110. New share = 40 ÷ 110 × 100 = 36.4%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A company budgeted income of £80 million and expenditure of £70 million. Actual income was 5% below budget and actual expenditure was 10% above budget. Calculate the profit variance.
items.why: Budgeted profit = £80m – £70m = £10m. Actual income = £76m, actual expenditure = £77m, so actual profit = –£1m (a loss). Variance = £10m – (–£1m) = £11m, adverse because profit is lower than budgeted.
items.label: Paper 1 November 2020 Q16

items.q: A business has capacity utilisation of 60%. It increases its capacity by 20% while output stays the same. What is its new capacity utilisation?
items.why: Take capacity as 100 units: output is 60. New capacity = 120. Utilisation = 60 ÷ 120 × 100 = 50%.

items.q: The table shows weekly output and total costs (0 units = £420, 1 = £700, 2 = £950, 3 = £1320, 4 = £1750). The total variable cost of producing three units of output is:
items.why: TVC = Total Cost - Fixed Costs. Fixed costs at zero output = £420. At 3 units, TC = £1320. So TVC = 1320 – 420 = £900. Students sometimes forget to subtract fixed costs. The cost at zero output IS the fixed cost.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business has non-current liabilities of £250,000 and gearing of 40%. It takes out a new long-term loan of £50,000. What is its new gearing?
items.why: Capital employed before = £250,000 ÷ 40% = £625,000. The loan adds to both non-current liabilities and capital employed. New gearing = (£250,000 + £50,000) ÷ (£625,000 + £50,000) × 100 = 44.4%.
items.label: New question
